description: Shaped Dirichlet noise (KataGo) on Go9 MLP 5iters

description: Policy surprise weighting λ=1.0 on Go9 MLP 25sims 5iters

description: C++ MCTS + MPS local: CNN 64f, 50 sims, playout cap, 4 workers
notes: 50s/iter locally (vs 170-300s with Python MCTS). C++ engine works great on Mac with MPS. Use for faster local iteration.

description: nn_batch_size=8 optimal for C++ engine (infra agent finding)
notes: nn_batch=64 causes batching overhead. Workers desynchronize with large batches → poor cross-worker batching. nn_batch=8 keeps workers in sync.

description: C++ MCTS 20 iters, CNN 64f, 50 sims, playout cap, 4 workers
notes: Loss steadily decreasing. vsR noisy (10-60% with 10 games). Entropy 1.3-2.0. Depth 4-6. Game length 94→46. ~60s/iter local. Model learning but still weak at 20 iters.

description: C++ ownership map collection — GoGame::get_ownership_map
notes: Ownership experiment can now use fast C++ MCTS path. Tested: 4-tuple examples with ownership shape (81,).

description: BS=64 vs BS=256 on C++ MCTS Go9 CNN 64f, 50 sims, 10 iters
notes: BS=256 clearly better: 13% lower total loss, policy 1.181 vs 1.389. Value loss identical (0.199). Larger batches = more stable gradients. Update GPU experiments to use BS=256.

description: Playout cap only (12.5% full, 87.5% cheap) on C++ MCTS Go9 CNN 64f, 50 sims, 30 games, 10 iters
notes: 17% higher loss due to fewer training examples (30 games × 12.5% = ~4 full positions/game). On GPU with 100+ games, playout cap gives equal quality at 4-5x speed. 37s/iter avg.

description: Policy target pruning thresh=0.03 on C++ MCTS Go9 CNN 64f, 50 sims, 30 games, 10 iters
notes: +6% vsRandom AND 9.3% lower loss (2.719 vs 2.999). KataGo technique confirmed: cleaner targets improve both loss and play strength. Added to all GPU experiments.

description: Progressive sims (25→100) vs constant 100 on C++ MCTS Go9 CNN 64f, 30 games, 10 iters
notes: Progressive 3.2% higher loss but 43% faster (551s vs 964s). Cost-efficiency better but quality slightly lower. Marginal at 10 iters — may help at GPU scale (300 iters). Not adding to GPU experiments yet.

description: Value loss weight 0.5 vs 1.0 on C++ MCTS Go9 CNN 64f, 50 sims, 30 games, 10 iters
notes: VLW=0.5 gives 7% better policy loss. Value identical (0.140 vs 0.138). vsRandom both 70% (too noisy at 10 iters/30 games). Added to GPU experiments — should compound over 300 iters.

description: Go9 500 iters, warm-start from Fix D, A5000
notes: 500 iters but plateaued at iter ~25. Loss ~1.75 for 475 iters. Old alpha=0.12. 3.6h, $0.58.

description: Go9 300 iters from scratch, alpha=0.03, c_puct=1.5, A5000
notes: Better than scale500 despite fewer iters. Plateaued ~1.65-1.80 after iter 86. 3.1h, $0.50.

description: Go9 200 iters, SE blocks + global pool, 6 res blocks, A5000
notes: BEST OF ALL. SE arch breaks through CNN plateau. Still improving at iter 176 (1.416). 3.4h, $0.54. 0/20 vs GnuGo L1 despite best loss.

description: Best GPU models vs GnuGo L1, 200 sims, 20 games each
notes: se_globalpool 0/20, scale500 0/20 vs GnuGo L1. Low loss ≠ playing strength. Need more training or architectural improvements.

description: Go9 300 iters, kitchen sink (PSW+VLW+shaped_dirichlet+liberty+pruning), A5000
notes: Plateau at 1.80 for 80 iters (18-100), then slow descent. PSW=0.5+VLW=0.5 hurt value head. SE arch > KataGo training tricks at this scale. 3.2h, $0.51.

description: 6 vs 10 SE+GP blocks on Go9 CNN 128f, 50 sims, 30 games, 5 iters
notes: 10b only 2.4% better but 43% slower (131s vs 91s/iter). 3.09M vs 1.88M params. Marginal at local scale — may help at GPU scale but not worth the cost increase.

description: 5 vs 10 epochs with SE+GP Go9 CNN 128f, 50 sims, 30 games, 5 iters
notes: **10 epochs is 47% better loss!** 1.337 in just 5 iters — comparable to se_globalpool's best at 137 iters. 236s/iter vs 149s/iter (+58% time). Much more learning per iteration.

description: Random opening moves 0 vs 6, SE+GP Go9 CNN 128f, 50 sims, 30 games, 5 iters
notes: ROM=6: 5.5% better loss AND 20% faster (676s vs 845s). Higher entropy (1.32 vs 0.51) = more diverse search. More balanced P1 wins (33-43% vs 13-47%). Diversity helps.

description: Epoch scaling: 10 vs 15 vs 20 on SE+GP Go9 CNN 128f, 50 sims, 30 games, 5 iters
notes: 10 epochs optimal. 15/20 epochs overfit — loss increases after iter 3-4. 1800 positions too small for 15+ epochs. 10 epochs is sweet spot for local buffer size.

description: c_puct 1.0 vs 2.0 on SE+GP 10ep Go9 CNN 128f, 50 sims, 30 games, 5 iters
notes: c_puct=1.5 confirmed optimal (1.337 from earlier test). 1.0 gives deeper search (4.4 vs 3.4) but less exploration. 2.0 wastes sims. Keep 1.5.

description: Buffer window 3 vs 5 on SE+GP 10ep Go9 CNN 128f, 50 sims, 30 games, 8 iters
notes: Both still decreasing at iter 8. w5 slightly better. w3 faster per iter (9s vs 17s). At 500 iters window matters more. Keep w10 for GPU (safer).

description: LR warmup=3 + cosine vs warmup=3 + constant, SE+GP 10ep, 8 iters
notes: Warmup HURTS. No-warmup constant gives 1.337 at 5 iters. Warmup wastes early iterations. Cosine too aggressive for short runs. Keep constant LR=0.001, no warmup.

description: Temp threshold 15 vs 60 on SE+GP 10ep Go9, 8 iters
notes: Only 3% difference. t15 gives lower entropy sooner (exploitation), t60 keeps exploring. Both similar. Keep t30 (current default).

description: Verbose games vs GnuGo L1 with se_globalpool best model
notes: ROOT CAUSE: (1) model passes prematurely (5 times in 1 game while GnuGo still playing), (2) groups get captured (no life/death reading), (3) massive territory losses (W+88.5, B+67.5). Ownership prediction should directly fix (1) and help (2).

description: SE+GP 10ep ROM, 50 sims, 30 games, 30 iters, local CPU
notes: Plateaus at ~1.5-1.6. Uptick after iter 19 (overfitting on small buffer). Local ceiling is ~1.5 at 50 sims/30 games. GPU needed for lower loss. 10ep reaches plateau in 10 iters vs 50 with 5ep.

description: Verbose games: local model vs random, GPU model vs random, GnuGo
notes: LOCAL MODEL: premature pass at move 31, enters infinite pass loop. Can't play Go beyond 30 moves. GPU MODEL: 10/10 vs random, plays full games (89-132 moves). Pass problem is training quality issue, not architectural. GPU model still 0/20 vs GnuGo — different problem (tactical depth).

description: Detailed GPU model vs GnuGo L1 game analysis
notes: ROOT CAUSE: life & death blindness. Model builds large frameworks (rootV=0.93) but groups aren't alive (no two eyes). GnuGo invades → captures everything → only 6/35 Black stones survive. Value head is blind to group vulnerability. Ownership prediction should fix this by teaching model which stones survive to game end.
